k: The old man. Harrow — he founded this Lodge. Something killed him in a hollow south of the moor. We never posted it. We never had anyone good enough.
src: 'The old man. Harrow — he founded this Lodge. Something killed him in a hollow south of the moor. We never posted it. We never had anyone good enough.'

k: You might be. I've marked the Hollow on your map. Don't make me take your names off the wall.
src: 'You might be. I\'ve marked the Hollow on your map. Don\'t make me take your names off the wall.'

k: Something killed the Lodge's founder. The Hollow is marked on the world map.
src: 'Something killed the Lodge\'s founder. The Hollow is marked on the world map.'

k: Every bounty. In a world like this. You know what that makes you? A reason for people to keep going.
src: 'Every bounty. In a world like this. You know what that makes you? A reason for people to keep going.'

k: There's one more. Not on any board. Up past the wounds, where the sky is darkest, something black hangs that isn't a wound.
src: 'There\'s one more. Not on any board. Up past the wounds, where the sky is darkest, something black hangs that isn\'t a wound.'

k: The old hunters called it the Black Star. I've marked the way. Be what you've been.
src: 'The old hunters called it the Black Star. I\'ve marked the way. Be what you\'ve been.'

k: Above the seven wounds hangs a dark star. The way is marked on the world map.
src: 'Above the seven wounds hangs a dark star. The way is marked on the world map.'

k: The chord sours. The tones fade. Something below sighs.
src: 'The chord sours. The tones fade. Something below sighs.'

k: The three tones become one. Far below, the great bell answers — and the way down opens.
src: 'The three tones become one. Far below, the great bell answers — and the way down opens.'

k: Antlers over the door. Smoke from the chimney. Somewhere inside, a woman is shouting at a ledger.
src: 'Antlers over the door. Smoke from the chimney. Somewhere inside, a woman is shouting at a ledger.'

k: Welcome to the Hunters' Lodge. I'm Adelind; I keep the board, the books and the peace, in that order.
src: 'Welcome to the Hunters\' Lodge. I\'m Adelind; I keep the board, the books and the peace, in that order.'

k: People post bounties for monsters that are too much for a village. You hunt them, you bring proof, you get paid. Proof is the monster not being there anymore.
src: 'People post bounties for monsters that are too much for a village. You hunt them, you bring proof, you get paid. Proof is the monster not being there anymore.'

k: Wipe your boots.
src: 'Wipe your boots.'

k: Lodge is open. Mostly. The roof's over there now.
src: 'Lodge is open. Mostly. The roof\'s over there now.'

k: I was Adelind's apprentice. She went down with the north wing when the sky broke. Kept the books dry, though. She'd want me to say that.
src: 'I was Adelind\'s apprentice. She went down with the north wing when the sky broke. Kept the books dry, though. She\'d want me to say that.'

k: The board still works. Monsters are worse. People need them gone more than ever.
src: 'The board still works. Monsters are worse. People need them gone more than ever.'

k: Oh — I know your face. You hunted for her. She used to say you never wiped your boots.
src: 'Oh — I know your face. You hunted for her. She used to say you never wiped your boots.'

k: At low tide a causeway rises out of the bay, and at its end a dome — half-sunk, green with weed, older than any Lantern.
src: 'At low tide a causeway rises out of the bay, and at its end a dome — half-sunk, green with weed, older than any Lantern.'

k: That's not on any map I've read.
src: 'That\'s not on any map I\'ve read.'

k: Then we're about to read a new one.
src: 'Then we\'re about to read a new one.'

k: The great lens throws a bar of light up the stair. The way is open.
src: 'The great lens throws a bar of light up the stair. The way is open.'

k: A great lens on a brass arm, crusted with salt. Beyond the gallery, the stairway is sealed by a curtain of pale crystal.
src: 'A great lens on a brass arm, crusted with salt. Beyond the gallery, the stairway is sealed by a curtain of pale crystal.'

k: Turn the lens toward the stair?
src: 'Turn the lens toward the stair?'

k: Sunlight bends through the glass and strikes the crystal. It sings — one clear note — and shatters.
src: 'Sunlight bends through the glass and strikes the crystal. It sings — one clear note — and shatters.'

k: That note. It is the one the Lanterns sing. But backwards.
src: 'That note. It is the one the Lanterns sing. But backwards.'

k: The orrery is still now. Seven brass suns, and one empty socket in the middle.
src: 'The orrery is still now. Seven brass suns, and one empty socket in the middle.'

k: A vast brass orrery fills the dome: seven small suns on seven arms, circling an empty socket.
src: 'A vast brass orrery fills the dome: seven small suns on seven arms, circling an empty socket.'

k: Carved around the rim: _WHAT IS SUNG FORWARD CAN BE SUNG BACK. WE MEASURED IT. WE CHOSE NOT TO._
src: 'Carved around the rim: _WHAT IS SUNG FORWARD CAN BE SUNG BACK. WE MEASURED IT. WE CHOSE NOT TO._'

k: "We chose not to." Who's we?
src: '"We chose not to." Who\'s we?'

k: The orrery's keeper wakes!
src: 'The orrery\'s keeper wakes!'

k: In the empty socket you find a book of measurements, written by the very first Keepers.
src: 'In the empty socket you find a book of measurements, written by the very first Keepers.'

k: The last page: _Seven voices hold the sun. Any one of them could stop it. That is why there must always be seven._
src: 'The last page: _Seven voices hold the sun. Any one of them could stop it. That is why there must always be seven._'

k: There was an observatory under the bay older than the Lanterns. The first Keepers knew the Dawnsong could be sung backwards. They chose not to.
src: 'There was an observatory under the bay older than the Lanterns. The first Keepers knew the Dawnsong could be sung backwards. They chose not to.'

k: Fort Ashwatch: an old Dawnguard frontier fort, abandoned for twenty years. The banners are rags. The gate is open.
src: 'Fort Ashwatch: an old Dawnguard frontier fort, abandoned for twenty years. The banners are rags. The gate is open.'

k: Ashwatch. Sir Aldous held this fort before he was my mentor. He said it was the coldest place he ever loved.
src: 'Ashwatch. Sir Aldous held this fort before he was my mentor. He said it was the coldest place he ever loved.'

k: A row of soldiers' graves, each marked with a Dawnguard sunburst. The newest is twenty years old.
src: 'A row of soldiers\' graves, each marked with a Dawnguard sunburst. The newest is twenty years old.'

k: Someone has been leaving wildflowers. Recently.
src: 'Someone has been leaving wildflowers. Recently.'

k: Sir Aldous's old office. The desk is empty now.
src: 'Sir Aldous\'s old office. The desk is empty now.'

k: A commander's office, frozen in the moment it was left. In the desk, an unsent letter, sealed, addressed in a square hand:
src: 'A commander\'s office, frozen in the moment it was left. In the desk, an unsent letter, sealed, addressed in a square hand:'

k: _To my squire, whoever he turns out to be._
src: '_To my squire, whoever he turns out to be._'

k: ...That's his handwriting.
src: '...That\'s his handwriting.'

k: He wrote it before he ever met me. "Whoever he turns out to be."
src: 'He wrote it before he ever met me. "Whoever he turns out to be."'

k: _If you are reading this, you are my squire, and you have just frozen in front of something terrible, and you think you are a coward._
src: '_If you are reading this, you are my squire, and you have just frozen in front of something terrible, and you think you are a coward._'

k: _I froze my first time too. In this fort. A man died covering for me. I have never told anyone._
src: '_I froze my first time too. In this fort. A man died covering for me. I have never told anyone._'

k: _Courage is not the part where you are not afraid. It is the part after. — A.V._
src: '_Courage is not the part where you are not afraid. It is the part after. — A.V._'

k: I'm fine. There's dust. In the fort. It's a very dusty fort.
src: 'I\'m fine. There\'s dust. In the fort. It\'s a very dusty fort.'

k: In Fort Ashwatch we found a letter Sir Aldous wrote to his future squire. Bram says the fort is very dusty.
src: 'In Fort Ashwatch we found a letter Sir Aldous wrote to his future squire. Bram says the fort is very dusty.'

k: An empty suit of commander's armor stands guard over the stairs. As you approach, it draws its sword.
src: 'An empty suit of commander\'s armor stands guard over the stairs. As you approach, it draws its sword.'

k: The armor kneels, slowly, as if relieved. The way to the signal tower is clear.
src: 'The armor kneels, slowly, as if relieved. The way to the signal tower is clear.'

k: The signal fire burns. Somewhere far off, you imagine, someone sees it.
src: 'The signal fire burns. Somewhere far off, you imagine, someone sees it.'

k: Light the old signal fire?
src: 'Light the old signal fire?'

k: The signal fire catches on the first try, as if it has been waiting twenty years for someone to bother.
src: 'The signal fire catches on the first try, as if it has been waiting twenty years for someone to bother.'

k: From the ashes beneath the grate you pull a commander's ring, warm as a hand.
src: 'From the ashes beneath the grate you pull a commander\'s ring, warm as a hand.'

k: The hollow is quiet. Wildflowers have started growing where the old man fell.
src: 'The hollow is quiet. Wildflowers have started growing where the old man fell.'

k: Bones, old and new. A hunter's horn, cracked. And in the dark at the back of the hollow, something that has been waiting a long time for someone worth eating.
src: 'Bones, old and new. A hunter\'s horn, cracked. And in the dark at the back of the hollow, something that has been waiting a long time for someone worth eating.'

k: Among the bones, Harrow's horn — still sound enough to blow. And a fang the length of your forearm.
src: 'Among the bones, Harrow\'s horn — still sound enough to blow. And a fang the length of your forearm.'

k: A shard of the old world, and beneath it, hanging by its roots like a seed-pod, the bell-tower of the Abbey of Hours — upside-down.
src: 'A shard of the old world, and beneath it, hanging by its roots like a seed-pod, the bell-tower of the Abbey of Hours — upside-down.'

k: Every few minutes, the bell inside it rings. No one is pulling the rope.
src: 'Every few minutes, the bell inside it rings. No one is pulling the rope.'

k: The bell remembers the order now. Go on down to her. Go gently.
src: 'The bell remembers the order now. Go on down to her. Go gently.'

k: You came down the tower? Upside down? Ha. Welcome to the Hollow Bell. I'm the sexton. I was the sexton. I am still, I think, the sexton.
src: 'You came down the tower? Upside down? Ha. Welcome to the Hollow Bell. I\'m the sexton. I was the sexton. I am still, I think, the sexton.'

k: There are three chimes in this nave. The bell below won't let anyone pass until they're rung in the old order. The order we rang for weddings.
src: 'There are three chimes in this nave. The bell below won\'t let anyone pass until they\'re rung in the old order. The order we rang for weddings.'

k: "Low for the promise, high for the joy, and the middle for every day after."
src: '"Low for the promise, high for the joy, and the middle for every day after."'

k: It's quiet. I didn't know it could be quiet. Thank you.
src: 'It\'s quiet. I didn\'t know it could be quiet. Thank you.'

k: Oh! People. Real ones. You're all the right way up.
src: 'Oh! People. Real ones. You\'re all the right way up.'

k: I'm Agathe. I ring the bell. I was ringing it when the sky broke, and the tower fell, and I just... kept ringing. In case anyone was still coming to the wedding.
src: 'I\'m Agathe. I ring the bell. I was ringing it when the sky broke, and the tower fell, and I just... kept ringing. In case anyone was still coming to the wedding.'

k: I can't stop. The bell won't let me. It thinks if it stops, everyone will be gone for real.
src: 'I can\'t stop. The bell won\'t let me. It thinks if it stops, everyone will be gone for real.'

k: Maybe they are. Maybe it's alright to let it be quiet.
src: 'Maybe they are. Maybe it\'s alright to let it be quiet.'

k: ...Will you ask it? It won't listen to me.
src: '...Will you ask it? It won\'t listen to me.'

k: The bell rings once more — softly, the way you ring a bell at the end of something — and goes still.
src: 'The bell rings once more — softly, the way you ring a bell at the end of something — and goes still.'
